summary.intent: Audit the entire web app for any other call sites of folderTree-dependent CipherBoxClient methods that are missing an ensureFolderRegistered guard — the same regression class as issue #494.
summary.outcome: A 7-agent parallel audit of 21 call sites confirmed only one additional gap: restoreFromBin in useBin.ts (lines 73 and 128). This was identified as a pre-existing bug from PR #296 (not the #494 regression). The #494 fix was verified green by the Web E2E suite, and the bin-restore architectural root cause was captured as a structured todo for a follow-up PR.

repo: shareFolder/revokeShare/reWrapForRecipients have zero web callers — web sharing goes through the REST API, not CipherBoxClient/folderTree.
useSharedWriteOps uses standalone SDK functions on a ref-built context, not CipherBoxClient methods, so it never touches folderTree.
The encrypt-worker.service.ts:102 uploadFiles reference is only a JSDoc comment, not an actual call site.
bin permanentDelete and emptyBin operate on bin records only, not folderTree — they are safe without a guard.
recycle-bin.spec.ts E2E always passes because it navigates/uploads first (parent already registered) and never reloads, so it structurally cannot catch the cold-reload restore bug.
The folderTree dependency in restoreFromBin dates to PR #296 — it is pre-existing, not a #494 regression.
CipherBoxClientConfig (packages/sdk/src/types.ts) carries rootIpnsName, rootFolderKey, and vaultKeypair but NOT rootIpnsKeypair — the root IPNS private key lives only in the web vaultStore.
The Zustand folder store is keyed by folder UUID (Record<string, FolderNode>), not ipnsName, and is populated only via navigation — never via bin operations.
The web app has no load-folder-by-ipnsName primitive; navigation loads incrementally from root using UUIDs. A complete fix for bin restore requires a from-root DFS resolver.

code.finding: restoreFromBin hard-throws 'Target folder not loaded' if folderTree.get(targetFolderIpnsName) returns undefined — no lazy-load, synchronous throw before any mutation.
restore() calls client.restoreFromBin(entryId, entry.originalParentIpnsName) with no preceding ensureFolderRegistered. Missing guard since PR #296.
restoreMultiple() loop calls client.restoreFromBin per entry with no ensureFolderRegistered — same defect as line 73.
Only imports getSdkClient and hasSdkClient from sdk-provider — ensureFolderRegistered is never imported.
restoreFromBin passes folderTree: this.folderTree straight into binOps.restoreFromBin with no internal guard or lazy-load.
folders: Record<string, FolderNode> is keyed by folder UUID, not ipnsName — looking up by ipnsName requires Object.values(folders).find(f => f.ipnsName === ...) (see line 212).
Canonical pattern for ipnsName lookup in the store: Object.values(folders).find((f) => f.ipnsName === targetIpnsName).

workflow: Grepping for getSdkClient().X( misses the aliased call style (const client = getSdkClient(); client.X(...)) — both patterns must be covered in call-site audits.
A multi-agent parallel audit workflow (5 family agents + adversarial verification) audited 21 call sites in ~3.75 min, far faster than sequential reads.
Distinguishing pre-existing bugs from regressions matters for PR scope: the #494 hotfix was kept clean so it could ship immediately; the pre-existing bin bug was captured as a follow-up todo.
Adversarial verification in the workflow caught the non-obvious wrinkle (store keyed by UUID, not ipnsName) that would have made a naive ensureFolderRegistered guard insufficient.

friction: Initial grep pattern (getSdkClient().X() style) missed aliased invocations, requiring a second grep pass to get the real call surface.

The full bin-restore fix is architecturally non-trivial: bin entries carry only originalParentIpnsName, the store is keyed by UUID, and a parent not navigated to this session is absent from both the store and folderTree — a simple guard closes only the common case.

The SDK client structurally cannot self-bootstrap because CipherBoxClientConfig omits the root IPNS private key — every folderTree-dependent method relies on the web to pre-seed folderTree, making the workaround class load-bearing.
The Web E2E result file was only partially readable inline (the audit output was truncated at 6237 chars), requiring a separate bash read of the full output file.
open_items: Fix useBin.ts:73 (restore) and useBin.ts:128 (restoreMultiple) to register the target parent folder before calling client.restoreFromBin — requires resolving FolderNode by ipnsName, and a full fix needs a load-parent-by-ipnsName path for the not-in-store case.

Architectural fix: add rootIpnsKeypair to CipherBoxClientConfig and implement an internal lazy ensureFolderLoaded(targetIpnsName) DFS-walker in CipherBoxClient, called inside all folderTree-dependent methods — this dissolves the entire ensureFolderRegistered workaround class.
New SDK unit test: ensureFolderLoaded with deep target, not-found target, and already-loaded target cases.
New web E2E test: reload → open bin → restore an item whose original parent subfolder was never navigated to in that session.
Open the verified #494 hotfix as its own PR (branch fix/owner-edit-folder-not-loaded, E2E green) before bundling the bin/architectural work.
